question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is 4 m and the area of the curved surface of the cylinder is 19.5 m², then its volume (in m³) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relation between **Volume (V)** and **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of a cylinder:

**Volume** = (**CSA** × **Radius**) ÷ 2

**Volume** = (19.5 × 4) ÷ 2

**Volume** = 78 ÷ 2 = 39 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 39 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius (r)** = 4 m

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 19.5 m²

**Formula Used:**

**Curved Surface Area** = 2πrh

**Volume** = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e60ae10c00fafe7c2c74501184b35bc22861483a1d50ae40c7b20821b92c412.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = 19.5

⇒ πh = 19.5 ÷ (2 × 4)

⇒ πh = 19.5 ÷ 8

⇒ **Volume** = πr²h

⇒ **Volume** = (r²) × (πh)

⇒ **Volume** = (4)² × (19.5 ÷ 8)

⇒ **Volume** = 16 × (19.5 ÷ 8)

⇒ **Volume** = 2 × 19.5 = 39 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 39 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

It includes the curved surface and the area of two circular bases: **TSA** = 2πr(h + r).

Volume and Area Relationship

For a cylinder, the ratio of **Volume** to **CSA** is always **r/2**.

Hollow Cylinder Volume

If R is outer and r is inner radius, **Volume** = π(R² − r²)h.</p
